title: A Slice One 279th the Size of This Worm Can Grow Into a Whole Worm

scenes.text: A worm piece one 279th the size can regrow a whole worm.
A biologist named Thomas Hunt Morgan chopped up these flatworms, called planarians, over a century ago.
He found a slice as small as one 279th could turn into a complete adult.
The secret is stem cells all through the body that can become almost any tissue.
Morgan got so frustrated by the mystery that he quit and studied fruit flies instead.
He later won a Nobel Prize for the flies.

description:
A slice as small as one 279th of a planarian flatworm can regrow into a whole adult.
Thomas Hunt Morgan reported it over a century ago. Planarians keep stem-like cells called neoblasts that can make any cell type the body needs.
What body part would you most want to regrow? Comment below.
first_comment: Morgan went on to win a Nobel Prize for his fruit fly work. Which would you have studied, the worms or the flies?
